reason: Putting the steel on the growing-room floor seems like a direct start on the bed structure.
expectation: I expect a frame or supports for the beds, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The reservoir and pump also need support, but I prefer to start with the main structure.

effect: The raised frames establish separate crop beds with outlets above the planned reservoir; lining them seems like the next structural step.
reaction: The different bed depths and drainage arrangement make the result feel purposeful.
reason: The liner should make the raised frames suitable for holding the growing beds.
expectation: I expect lined beds, though I don't know whether they will be ready for planting yet.

alternatives.reason: The reservoir and pump also need installation, but I want to finish the bed structure first.

effect: The beds now hold solution while their drain fittings remain usable; they still need irrigation connections.
reaction: The distinction between the load-bearing frame and liner is clear and satisfying.
reason: The reservoir and pump need a support beneath the bed outlets.
expectation: I expect a supported reservoir and pump, ready to connect to the beds.

alternatives.reason: The hose could connect the beds, but I want the reservoir in place first.

effect: The reservoir is supported and ready for a hose connection.
reaction: The result is straightforward, though it gives no detail about the support.
reason: Connecting the hose to the reservoir seems like a practical next step toward irrigation.
expectation: I expect a hose-connected reservoir, though I am unsure how it will connect to the beds.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the hose to the beds first, but I chose the reservoir end.

effect: The reservoir return aerates the solution before it is pumped back; the beds still need their hose connection.
reaction: The small falling return is a clear, useful detail I hadn't expected.
reason: The hose-to-beds connection is the only offered gameplay action and should advance the irrigation setup.
expectation: I expect the beds to gain an irrigation connection, though I don't know whether the whole system will be complete.

effect: The beds now drain toward the reservoir, completing the structure; the next goal is to connect the return system.
reaction: The gravity-fed drains make the purpose of the raised beds clear.
reason: This is the only offered gameplay action and should connect the beds to the aerating reservoir.
expectation: I expect a connected recirculating system, though it may still need water or further preparation.

effect: The beds and reservoir now form a shared distribution and return system, with separate adjustments for each crop; the chapter is complete.
reaction: The shared pump alongside individually adjustable root zones is a satisfying practical detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the beds and reservoir brought the separate drainage and irrigation pieces together into a coherent system.

leastWorthwhile.text: Supporting the reservoir was straightforward but offered little detail about how the support worked.

surprise.text: The falling return aerates the solution before it is pumped back, an unexpectedly simple detail.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly purposeless, though attaching the hose to the reservoir did not initially make its aerating role obvious.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the different beds are prepared for crops, especially after learning how the shared system handles drainage and aeration.
